Start over

Destructive

Forgotten the passphrase? Nobody can reset it for you — that is what makes the guarantee real. Generating a new key gets messaging working again from today, and permanently gives up every message sent before now. Not "hidden": unreadable, by anyone, forever.

{% else %} {# ------------------------------------------------------ first time run #}

Set a message passphrase

Not set up

Pick a passphrase. Your browser will generate a key pair, encrypt the private half with it, and upload only the encrypted result. The passphrase itself is never sent — not at sign-up, not at sign-in, not ever.

Deliberately not your account password. The server has to see your account password when you sign in. A vault locked with a password the server sees would be a vault the server can open. Use something different, and write it down somewhere safe — there is no reset.
Longer beats complicated. Four unrelated words is fine.

{% endif %}

What this does and doesn't cover

Direct messages Encrypted end to end. The server stores ciphertext and has no key.
Who you messaged, and when Stored in the clear. Delivering a message means knowing where to send it — no design avoids this.
Public rooms Not encrypted, and can't be. Open membership means no key that only the participants hold.
Comments, likes, history Stored in plain text on this server, same as they always were.
Old messages if your passphrase leaks Exposed. One long-lived key per account — there's no forward secrecy in this design.

The full version of this is on the privacy page.
